@app.nav.capture.description: Navigation item and page title. Capture means taking over this PC's keyboard and mouse to control another device.

@app.common.exit.description: Button and tray menu item that closes BLE HID completely.

app.status.description: Publish the keyboard and mouse services, then pair from the device you want to control.
app.status.notAdvertising.title: Not advertising

@app.status.notAdvertising.title.description: Warning title: other devices cannot currently find this PC over Bluetooth.

app.status.notAdvertising.message: Start the peripheral to make this PC discoverable as a Bluetooth keyboard.

@app.status.peripheral.description: Card title. A peripheral is the Bluetooth keyboard and mouse that this PC pretends to be.

@app.status.advertisement.description: {status} is one of the advertisement texts, e.g. Started.

app.status.encryption.title: Require encryption
app.status.encryption.description: Hosts must bond before they can read reports. Can only be changed while stopped.

@app.status.encryption.description.description: A host is a paired phone, tablet or computer that receives input. To bond means to pair securely.

@app.status.keyboardSubscribers.description: Number of connected hosts that currently receive keyboard input.

@app.status.mouseSubscribers.description: Number of connected hosts that currently receive mouse input.

@app.status.logs.description: Heading above technical log messages, which stay in English.

@advertisement.created.description: Bluetooth advertising state: prepared but not running yet.

@advertisement.aborted.description: Bluetooth advertising state: Windows stopped it unexpectedly.

@advertisement.partial.description: Bluetooth advertising state: running, but some of the advertised details were left out.

app.capture.description: Redirect this PC's keyboard and mouse to a paired host.
app.capture.redirecting.title: Capture takes over this PC
app.capture.redirecting.message: While input is going to a host, this window stops receiving it. Press {stopShortcut} to stop capture, or {switchShortcut} to switch to the next target.

@app.capture.redirecting.message.description: {stopShortcut} and {switchShortcut} are keyboard shortcuts, built from the key.* names.

app.capture.noHosts.title: No hosts yet
app.capture.noHosts.message: Pair from the device you want to control, then wait for it to subscribe. On a Windows host, pick the entry shown as an input device rather than the audio one.

@app.capture.sendingTo.description: {target} is a device name, or one of the target texts.

app.capture.lockWarning: Lock keys on the target host

@app.capture.lockWarning.description: Warning title shown when Caps Lock or Num Lock is in an unexpected state on the device being controlled.

@app.capture.pointer.description: Section heading for mouse pointer settings.

app.capture.pointerInterval.title: Minimum pointer interval
app.capture.pointerInterval.description: Paced to {interval} ms right now — whichever is slower of this minimum and the connection interval the host negotiated.

@app.capture.milliseconds.description: {value} is a number of milliseconds. Use your language's abbreviation for milliseconds if it differs.

@app.capture.switchShortcutAlternative.description: Shown under the main shortcut. {shortcut} is an alternative keyboard shortcut.

app.target.thisPc.title: This PC
app.target.thisPc.detail: Capture stays armed but keystrokes are passed through locally.

@target.local.description: Inserted into app.capture.sendingTo and the tray tooltip.

@target.allHosts.description: Inserted into app.capture.sendingTo: input goes to every connected device at once.

@target.none.description: Inserted into app.capture.sendingTo before Bluetooth has started.

@lock.capsOn.description: Warning about the controlled device. Capital letters are used to stand out.

lock.capsOnNumOff: CAPS LOCK ON, NUM LOCK OFF
app.settings.description: Control how BLE HID starts and what happens when the window is closed.
app.settings.autoStartUnavailable.title: Auto-start unavailable
app.settings.autoStartUnavailable.messag: Run the published executable rather than 'dotnet run' to register auto-start.

@app.settings.autoStartUnavailable.messa.description: Developer-only message. Keep 'dotnet run' as written.

app.settings.startWithWindows.title: Start with Windows
app.settings.startWithWindows.descriptio: Launches hidden in the notification area when you sign in.
app.settings.startPeripheral.title: Start the peripheral automatically
app.settings.startPeripheral.description: Begins advertising as soon as the app launches.
app.settings.keepRunning.title: Keep running when the window is closed
app.settings.keepRunning.description: Paired hosts reconnect to a peripheral that never restarted, so staying resident keeps them working.
app.settings.gesture.title: Shake the pointer to switch target
app.settings.gesture.description: Move the mouse rapidly back and forth to cycle between this PC and the paired hosts. {switchShortcut} always works too.
app.settings.language.title: Language
app.settings.language.description: Takes effect the next time BLE HID starts.

@app.settings.language.system.description: Language option that follows the language Windows is set to.

app.settings.exit.title: Exit BLE HID
app.settings.exit.description: Stops advertising and removes the tray icon. Hosts will need to reconnect.

@app.tray.lockKeys.description: Notification title for the Caps Lock and Num Lock warnings.

app.tray.stillRunning: Still running. Right-click the tray icon to exit.
app.dialog.alreadyRunning:
BLE HID is already running, either in the notification area or as the command line background service.

Stop it and continue?

@app.dialog.alreadyRunning.description: \n starts a new line; keep it.

app.dialog.tooOldToStop: The running instance is too old to accept a stop request. Exit it manually.
app.dialog.didNotStop: The running instance did not stop in time.

@app.dialog.unexpectedError.description: {message} is a technical error in English; {path} is a file path.

@key.ctrl.description: The Ctrl key as printed on keyboards in your language, e.g. Strg in German. Every shortcut in BLE HID is built from this name.

@key.capsLock.description: The Caps Lock key as Windows names it in your language, e.g. Feststelltaste in German. Used in shortcuts.

@common.on.description: State of a setting or a lock key.

@common.off.description: State of a setting or a lock key.

@cli.startupFailed.description: {message} is a technical error in English.

@cli.ready.status.description: {status} is one of the advertisement texts, e.g. Started.

cli.ready.pair: Pair from your phone's Bluetooth settings, then use the commands below.

@cli.help.type.description: Help for a command-line command. The commands themselves stay in English.

cli.help.key: press a named key (enter, esc, up, f5, ...)

@cli.help.key.description: Keep the key names in brackets in English: they are what you type.

cli.help.capture: redirect the local keyboard and mouse ({stopShortcut} stops)
cli.help.captureInterval: same, with a custom pointer report interval
cli.help.host: list subscribed hosts and the current target
cli.help.hostSelect: choose the target; local keeps input on this PC

@cli.help.hostSelect.description: Keep the word local in English: it is what you type.

cli.help.gestureToggle: shake the pointer to switch target; applies to a running session
cli.help.status: show subscriber counts and the target's lock keys
cli.help.appearance: advertise GAP appearance = keyboard (no effect on this stack)

@cli.help.appearance.description: Developer diagnostic. GAP appearance is a Bluetooth term; keep it.

cli.help.watch: log connection and subscription changes as they happen
cli.help.probe: try to create a GATT service, e.g. probe 1801
cli.help.l2cap: test if user mode can listen on Classic HID L2CAP PSMs

@cli.help.l2cap.description: Developer diagnostic full of Bluetooth terms; keep the terms.

cli.help.classic: toggle BR/EDR connectable (fails with E_INVALIDARG on this stack)
cli.help.backgroundTitle: Background mode (keeps hosts bonded across restarts):
cli.help.background: run detached, without a console; same capture shortcuts
cli.help.lang: show messages in another language, e.g. --lang de
cli.noSubscriber: no subscriber yet - connect a host first

@cli.sendError.description: {message} is a technical error in English.

@cli.error.description: {message} is a technical error in English.

@cli.type.skipped.description: The type command can only send characters on a US keyboard layout.

cli.usage.probe: usage: probe <4-digit hex uuid>, e.g. probe 1801

@cli.usage.probe.description: Translate the words in angle brackets; keep the command.

@cli.usage.gesture.description: Keep on and off in English: they are what you type.

@cli.host.sendingTo.description: {target} is a device name, or one of the target texts.

@cli.host.inferred.description: {locks} is a lock-key warning. Inferred: guessed from the keys sent, because the host did not report it.

@cli.gesture.saveFailed.description: {error} is a technical error in English.

@cli.gesture.state.description: {state} is the common.on or common.off text.

@cli.gesture.tuning.description: How the shake gesture is detected: the pointer must change direction {reversals} times, moving at least {pixels} pixels each time, within {milliseconds} milliseconds.

@cli.status.advertisement.description: Row label in the status command; keep labels short.

@cli.status.onAlert.description: Caps Lock is on: written in capitals because it is the state that surprises people.

@cli.status.offAlert.description: Num Lock is off: written in capitals because it is the state that surprises people.

@cli.status.measured.description: The lock state was reported by the host itself.

@cli.status.inferred.description: The lock state was guessed from the keys sent, because the host did not report it.

cli.status.brEdrPeers: Classic Bluetooth devices ({count}) - only a problem if a host is missing from the subscribers:
cli.background.alreadyRunning: BleHid is already running in the background.
cli.autostart.noRunKey: Could not open the Windows Run registry key.
cli.autostart.devBuild: Run this from the published executable, not via 'dotnet run'.

@cli.autostart.installed.description: {command} is the command line Windows will run at sign-in.

@android.app_name.description: Android app name. Usually kept as is; translate only the word Companion if that is common in your language.

@android.monitor_notification_channel.description: Notification category name shown in Android settings.

android.monitor_notification_text: Keeping a diagnostic Bluetooth connection active

@android.allow_nearby_devices.description: Button that asks for Android's Nearby devices permission; use the name Android uses for that permission.

@android.state_idle.description: Short status badge, written in capitals where your language has them.

@android.section_database.description: Section heading. GATT is a Bluetooth term; keep it.

@android.metric_reports.description: Number of keyboard and mouse report channels found. Keep it short: it labels a small tile.

@android.metric_hash.description: A fingerprint of the computer's Bluetooth service list. Keep it short.

@android.metric_changed.description: Tile label: how many times the computer said its services changed.

@android.metric_presence.description: Tile label: whether the computer is nearby.

@android.hash_saved.description: The fingerprint was seen for the first time and stored.

@android.hash_same.description: The fingerprint matches the stored one.

@android.hash_changed.description: The fingerprint differs from the stored one.

@android.connect_input.description: Button that asks Android to reconnect the computer as a keyboard and mouse.

android.settings_required: Android {version} requires system settings to reconnect the input profile.

@android.settings_required.description: {version} is an Android version number such as 16.

@android.section_events.description: Section heading above the list of connection events, which stay in English.
